equity_bridge.item: Cat Financial / Financial Products at 1.5x attributable book
equity_bridge.note: Financial Products equity 5,431 at 2026-09-30 less 68 NCI = 5,363 x 1.5. FP ROE ~16% (FY2025 profit 733 on avg equity ~4,540; 9M-2026 639). Justified P/B at 9.5-10% CoE and 3% growth is ~1.8x; 1.5x haircuts for credit-cycle and funding risk.

equity_bridge.item: MP&E intercompany loans to Financial Products
equity_bridge.note: Eliminated debt between MP&E and FP: 1,299 long-term (consolidating adjustment on LTD) + 500 short-term borrowings with consolidated companies, 2026-09-30 10-Q. FP's book equity is net of this debt, so MP&E's claim is a separate asset at par.
MP&E liability for postemployment benefits 3,609 at 2026-09-30 x (1 - 23%). Debt-like; service cost is inside EBITDA, the deficit is not.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.75% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 27.96% and revenue 10.12%: equity is depressed by ~$22bn of buybacks FY2021-9M2026 (treasury stock -56.7bn), and FY2020 EPS (5.51) is a COVID trough. Neither CAGR is a forward growth rate; the scenario paths are built from guidance (2024-2030 enterprise sales CAGR target 6-9%) and an explicit cycle instead.
historical_growth.notes: Consolidated basis FY2020/FY2022 -> FY2025. Owner FCF = consolidated FCF (OCF - capex ex equipment leased to others) - SBC; SBC is ~0.35% of revenue so the SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are essentially identical -- SBC is not funding the growth. FY2025 revenue 67,589, EPS 18.90 (diluted 18.81 per 10-K), equity 21,318.

scenario_narratives.base: Backlog converts: FY2027-28 grow 7% and 5% as reciprocating-engine and turbine capacity ramps into data-center and prime-power orders already booked into 2029-30, while North American construction (IIJA, data-center sites) and a copper/gold-led mining fleet replacement hold up. Tariffs (~2.2bn in 2026) are partly priced through, so margins recover to ~23% at the 2028 peak. Then the machinery cycle does what it always does: dealer destocking and a construction/mining slowdown take FY2029-30 sales down ~6% from peak and margin to 20.5%, cushioned by a Power Gen book that is contracted and a services annuity. Mid-cycle 22.5% EBITDA margin and GDP-plus growth are what gets capitalized -- not the 2026-28 peak.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI/data-center power is a decade-long structural build, not a capex bubble: Power Generation reaches >3x 2024 sales by 2030 as targeted, turbines and large recips stay capacity-constrained with pricing power, and the downturn in construction and mining is shallow and offset by P&E. Sales compound ~9% to 2029 (above the 6-9% target band), mix lifts mid-cycle EBITDA margin to ~24%, tariff costs are mitigated by price and footprint, and the elevated 2027-29 capex earns full returns.
scenario_narratives.bear: Two cycles turn together: hyperscaler capex is cut in 2027-28 and the 78bn backlog proves softer than it looks (cancellations, pushed-out deliveries), just as construction and mining roll over on weaker commodity prices and dealer inventory unwinds (the Q4-2026 1.6bn seasonal destock is the preview). MP&E sales fall ~24% peak-to-trough into FY2029 -- still milder than 2015-16's 42% -- with the just-built ~3x engine capacity sitting under-utilized (D&A up, margin to ~17.5%), tariffs persisting under Section 232/122, and Chinese OEMs (XCMG, Sany) taking share in emerging markets. Recovery is ordinary and mid-cycle margin settles at 20.5%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the industrial business on its own owner cash flows through a full cycle, and the captive lender as a lender. Caterpillar is priced off a peak-year backlog; the house case refuses to capitalize peak margins or peak volumes and instead runs a normal downturn inside the ten-year horizon, then capitalizes mid-cycle cash flow at a cyclical 15x cap. Cat Financial is valued at a haircut to its justified P/B rather than through a consolidated DCF that would mistake its receivable-funding debt for corporate leverage.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI/data-center power demand durability: the P&E backlog and the 2027-29 capacity build both assume it persists; bull and bear diverge mainly here.
Cycle timing: a downturn placed in FY2029-30 is a judgment; an earlier or deeper one (2015-16 saw -42% revenue) moves value materially.
Mid-cycle margin: each 1pp of EBITDA margin across the forecast is roughly $13-15/share.

Terminal cap binds at 15x in every scenario (Gordon at 9%/3% is ~17.2x, so lifting the cap adds at most ~8%); closing the gap to the price needs a lower discount rate or structurally higher margins -- the market price embeds a non-cyclical multiple on peak-ish earnings.
Tariff regime (Section 232 steel/aluminum, Section 122 global) and further IEEPA recoveries are unmodelled upside/downside around a ~2.2bn annual cost.
Cat Financial credit cycle: valued at 1.5x book; a credit loss cycle coinciding with the machinery downturn would cut that.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 537.08-1073.46. No split in the window -- the fall from the high is a genuine drawdown (weekly closes ~1,000 in late June to the current level in early November).
data_sources.financials: CAT 10-K FY2023-FY2025 and 10-Q Q1-2024 through Q3-2026 (SEC EDGAR), specifically the Supplemental Consolidating Data (MP&E vs Financial Products) for results, financial position and cash flow; Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL) for consolidated history and CAGRs.
data_sources.qualitative: CAT_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): segments, backlog 78.1bn, FY2026 guidance (S&R +mid-to-high teens, tariffs ~2.2bn, MP&E capex ~3.3bn, ETR ~23%), 2024-2030 6-9% enterprise CAGR target, ~3x large recip capacity by 2030.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E Machinery, Power & Energy (MP&E) sales only: 9M-2026 actual 55,708 (Q3-2026 10-Q supplemental consolidating data) + Q4-2026E 19,650 (Q4-2025 MP&E 18,202 x ~1.08: P&E 'moderate' growth, CI 'similar', RI 'strong' per Q3 outlook). Implies consolidated S&R ~79.3bn, +17% -- inside the 'mid-to-high teens' FY2026 guide. Financial Products revenue is excluded from the flows; Cat Financial is valued separately in the equity bridge.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: ~458m basic shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q liquidity section) + ~2m treasury-method award dilution (Q3 diluted 460.9m weighted). Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows; buybacks (7.745bn in 9M-2026) are the cash mechanism, value-neutral in this model.
inputs.net_debt_note: MP&E only at 2026-09-30: long-term debt 10,913 + current portion 36 less MP&E cash 7,102. Cat Financial's ~35.5bn of debt funds its finance receivables and is netted inside its book equity (valued in equity_bridge) -- consolidated debt is NOT net debt for the industrial business.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 MP&E operating cash flow 12,278 less MP&E capex 2,758 and equipment leased to others 36 (FY2025 10-K supplemental cash flow). Consolidated FY2025 FCF in Metrics.csv is 8,918 (OCF 11,739 - capex ex-leased 2,821).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K stock-based compensation expense 242 (equity note, line 6954). Tax withheld on net-share settlement is netted inside 'Common stock issued, and other stock compensation transactions, net' (-16 FY2025, -131 9M-2026) with exercise proceeds and is not separately disclosed; the expense line is used.
inputs.buyback_note: 9M-2026 cash repurchases 7,745 (FY2025 5,190; FY2024 7,697). Active repurchaser: the flat count is funded. 7.19bn left on the 2024 authorization at 2026-09-30.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate: 10y UST ~4.3% + beta ~1.05 x 5.0% ERP = cost of equity ~9.5%; MP&E carries only ~3.8bn net debt against ~260bn market cap, so WACC ~9.0%. Same 9.0% in all three scenarios: cyclical and AI-power risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are immaterial for MP&E (US GAAP, lease cost inside COGS/SG&A and therefore inside EBITDA); no lease liability in net debt. One treatment, charged once.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component build) on the industrial business (MP&E) + Cat Financial valued separately at a multiple of book in the equity bridge -- a sum-of-parts per dcf-methods SKILL.md ('straddles two rows'). A captive finance arm is a lender: its debt is operating funding, its flows are post-interest, and running consolidated FCF against consolidated net debt (~33bn) would charge ~25bn of finance-receivable funding against the industrial EV. The 10-K/10-Q supplemental consolidating data splits MP&E and Financial Products cleanly, so every flow, balance and bridge item here is the MP&E column. The ~500m/yr dividend Cat Financial pays MP&E (inside MP&E OCF / other income) is excluded from the component flows because its source asset is in the bridge (adaptations rule d). MP&E net interest is not in the flows (unlevered build); MP&E debt and cash are in net_debt. Balance sheet is 2026-09-30 while fy0 is FY2026E: Q4-2026 cash generation is neither in net debt nor in the flows (conservative by roughly one quarter of FCF, ~$5-7/share). Cyclicality: FY2026 is a record year (backlog 78.1bn, Power Gen +30%) -- the base case deliberately runs a 2029-30 downturn and capitalizes a mid-cycle margin, not the peak; the terminal cap is 15x (cyclical) rather than 20x.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +7% off the 78.1bn backlog and capacity ramp (management: capacity, not demand, is the P&E constraint); +5% FY2028 lands FY2028 MP&E ~85bn, roughly on the top half of the 6-9% 2024-2030 enterprise CAGR target. Then a normal-sized machinery downturn (FY2029 flat-ish, FY2030 -6%; far milder than 2015-16's -42% because Power Gen is now ~half of sales and largely contracted) before recovering to GDP-plus.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: EBITDA before SBC on MP&E sales. FY2025 19.7% (tariff-hit), FY2024 23.9%, 9M-2026 23.0% incl. ~520m of one-off IEEPA recoveries (~0.9pp). Ex recoveries ~22%; tariff mitigation and P&E mix lift to 23% at the 2028 peak, deleverage to 20.5% in the downturn, mid-cycle 22.5% capitalized.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 MP&E capex guide ~3.3bn (4.4%). Large reciprocating-engine capacity to ~3x 2024 by 2030 with spending concentrated 2027-2029 -> ~5% through 2029, then back to a maintenance-plus 3.0% (vs D&A 2.8%) once the new capacity is depreciating.
base.tax_rationale: Guided ETR ~23% ex discrete; FY2025 cash taxes 2,206 on PBT 11,541 (~19%). 22% cash rate on unlevered EBIT.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer: MP&E receivables + inventory (27.2bn) less payables and customer advances (15.8bn) ~= 11.4bn net, ~15% of TTM sales. Growth consumes cash, downturns release it -- capture is negative on the change in revenue. Dealer/customer receivables financed by Cat Financial grow inside FP's balance sheet, funded by FP retention.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: FY2026 is a record year at the top of a classic machinery cycle and a large slice of the backlog and capex plan rests on one demand source (AI/data-center power) whose durability is unproven -- the stock's ~45% fall from its 52-week high is the market pricing exactly that. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right (AI capex persists, construction/mining stay strong, tariffs fade). Base at 50% is the backlog-converts-then-normal-downturn path. No balance-sheet or refinancing risk motivates the bear weight: MP&E net debt is ~3.8bn.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
